answer: The ridge detector writes to signal, and kernel exposes every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 235 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 82 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 22 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
